widgets.name: Block
widgets.summary: A bordered, titled, padded rectangle that other widgets draw inside.
widgets.note: A Block draws chrome only — it has no children. What goes inside it is the application's business: wrap a widget, or use a Split to place several. The capture shows the padding and the interior band, which is the part of the widget that is actually drawn.

widgets.name: Text
widgets.summary: A single line of styled spans, aligned within its rectangle.

widgets.name: Paragraph
widgets.summary: Wrapped, styled prose that reflows to the width it is given.

widgets.name: Split
widgets.summary: A container that divides its rectangle among focusable panes.
widgets.note: Focus moves between panes with Tab and the focused pane is the one that takes keys. A still frame cannot show that; the marker in the second pane's title is where the capture has to stop.

widgets.name: TextInput
widgets.summary: A single-line editable field with a cursor, a selection and undo.
widgets.note: This capture is taken with the field focused, so the cursor mark is live.

widgets.name: TextArea
widgets.summary: A multi-line editable field with wrapping, selection and undo.

widgets.name: Select
widgets.summary: A single-choice control that expands into a scrollable list.
widgets.note: A Select draws its options below the field rather than over the page, so the capture shows ten of the ten labels with the fifth highlighted.

widgets.name: Checkbox
widgets.summary: A tri-state box: unchecked, checked, or indeterminate.
widgets.note: Indeterminate is never produced by toggling. Only an application that has computed it from its children can set it, so the capture sets it directly.

widgets.name: Radio
widgets.summary: A single-choice group of labels, navigated with the arrow keys.

widgets.name: Toggle
widgets.summary: A two-state switch with an on and an off rendering.

widgets.name: Tabs
widgets.summary: A horizontal strip of labels, one of which is the active pane.

widgets.name: Button
widgets.summary: A labelled, activatable control with a default and a disabled state.

widgets.name: KeyHint
widgets.summary: A one-line bar of key names and their meanings.
widgets.note: At 40 columns the bar has fewer cells than bindings, so it drops the lowest-priority ones rather than truncating mid-word. That trade is visible in the narrow capture.

widgets.name: List
widgets.summary: A scrollable, selectable list with a marker gutter and a scrollbar.
widgets.note: The scrollbar thumb's POSITION is the signal; its colour is not.

widgets.name: Table
widgets.summary: Rows in columns, with a header, a selection and horizontal scrolling.

widgets.name: Tree
widgets.summary: A hierarchy with expandable nodes, keyboard navigation and lazy row rendering.
widgets.note: Expansion is state, and a still frame shows it only by the twisties and the indent. The example program is where a reader sees a node open.

widgets.name: Pager
widgets.summary: A scrollable long text with search, match highlighting and a position readout.

widgets.name: ProgressBar
widgets.summary: A ratio from 0 to 1 drawn as a filled block-element bar.
widgets.note: Filled with U+2588 FULL BLOCK. The difference between FillStyle and TrackStyle carries an attribute as well as a colour, so the bar is readable without either.

widgets.name: Gauge
widgets.summary: A bounded reading drawn as a Braille dial or a fallback bar.
widgets.note: The dial is Braille, U+2800..28FF: eight levels of vertical resolution in each cell, two samples per cell. A web font that gives those glyphs a different advance width destroys the arc, which is why the plain-text capture beside it is mandatory rather than a nicety.

widgets.name: Meter
widgets.summary: A budget with named zones, a threshold marker and the active zone's name in words.
widgets.note: Two non-colour signals: the zone boundaries are drawn as '+', the threshold as '|', and the active band is named in text.

widgets.name: Sparkline
widgets.summary: A series of numbers drawn as Braille or block elements, scaled to its own range.
widgets.note: Braille encoding, two samples per cell, so the series holds twice the values the width can show. The threshold defaults to reverse video, which is an attribute rather than a colour.

widgets.name: BarChart
widgets.summary: Categorical magnitudes as horizontal or vertical bars, with an axis and per-bar values.
widgets.note: Bars are Block Elements. The value beside each bar is the colour-independent reading and the capture keeps it.

widgets.name: Menu
widgets.summary: A navigable menu with nested submenus to arbitrary depth.
widgets.note: The selected item and any open branch are marked with a character and a rule, not colour alone. Depth beyond one submenu is available but not shown here.

widgets.name: Dialog
widgets.summary: A modal box with a title, a body and a row of actions.
widgets.note: Modal: keys do not reach the tree beneath. The focused action is ringed rather than coloured - a bracket pair of the same width as the idle pair, so moving focus never reflows the row - and reinforced with reverse video, which survives NO_COLOR because colour is suppressed only at encode time. Escape is Cancel, never a no-op.
